Preface
1.

Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with judgment dated 24.05.2018 passed by the Claims Tribunal, respondent TATA AIG General Insurance Company Ltd and injured Sandeep Thapa filed their separate appeals under section 173 of M.V. Act which have been disposed by common order dated 03.11.2020 passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi.

entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
2. MAC.APP No.772/2018 assailing the award by contending that motorcycle No.HR-26BN-3981 insured with TATA AIG General Insurance Company was not involved in the accident has been dismissed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi whereas MAC.APP No.180/2020 seeking compensation on the basis of 'Disability Certificate' issued by J.P.N. Apex Trauma Centre,
AIIMS has been disposed granting liberty to injured to approach the Tribunal for reconsideration of his claim for compensation for permanent disability.
Background 3.

Succinctly stated, injured Sandeep Thapa driving motorcycle No. DL-3SAR-9123 on his way from Gurgaon to Dhaula Kuan sustained grievous injury in motor vehicle accident near Sanjay T-Point Flyover, Delhi Cantt. on 18.11.2011 at about 9:30 pm after being hit by offending motorcycle No.HR-26BN- 3981 coming from behind at very high speed in rash and negligent manner.

It is submitted that accident took place as a result of rash and negligent driving of offending motorcycle and injured having suffered permanent disability is entitled to be compensated for general and special damages consequent to injuries sustained in road accident.
Inquiry And Finding 4.

R1/Pramod Kumar (driver) and R2/Sh. Narayan Singh (owner) of motorcycle No.HR-99-KJ (Temp)-7548 (permanent) No. HR-26-BN-3981 chose to suffer ex-parte proceedings after substituted service through publication in 'Veer Arjun' dated 06.12.2013 whereas R3/TATA AIG General Insurance Company Ltd. has disputed its liability to pay compensation by denying involvement of motorcycle in the alleged accident.

Treatment; (ii) Rs.40,000/- towards conveyance; (iii) Rs.30,000/- towards special diet; (iv)
Rs.60,000/- towards Nursing/Attendant/Physiotherapy; (v) Rs.40,000/- towards loss of income;
(vi) Rs.50,000/- towards mental and physical shock; (vii) Rs.1,50,000/- towards Pain and Suffering AND (viii) Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Further Inquiry apropos Compensation for 'Permanent Disability'
9.

Application for directing Medical Superintendent, DDU Hospital, Hari Nagar, Delhi to examine Sandeep Thapa was allowed on 19.04.2021 whereas 'Disability Certificate' assessing 18% (eighteen percent) disability in relation to both upper limbs has been proved as Ex. PW-3/1 by Dr. Vineet Arora, Senior Specialist, Orthopedic Department, DDU, New Delhi who has deposed that aforesaid disability is in respect of both upper limbs only and not in respect of the whole body during cross- examination by Ld. counsel for insurance Company.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME/PROSPECTS 10.

Disability Certificate Ex.PW-3/1 issued by Medical Board, DDU Hospital pursuant to order dated 19.04.2021 describes injured Sandeep Thapa as case of 'Bilateral Post Traumatic Post Operated Bilateral Fracture Shaft of Humrous with Implant in situ with Stiffness of Shoulder Joints with Permanent Physical Disability of 18% (Eighteen Percent) in relation to Both Upper Limb.
11.

permanent disability on the actual earning capacity would involve three steps as laid down in para 13 of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India titled Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar (Supra).
12. What is required to be assessed by the Tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earning by applying the standard multiplier method used to determine the loss of dependency as held in para 11 of aforesaid judgment titled Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar (Supra).
13. Considering the age and ability of injured to carry on some other or lesser scale of activities, this Court is of the opinion that permanent physical disability of 18% in relation to both upper limb could have resulted in 10% functional disability towards loss of earning capacity of injured.

14. Injured Sandeep Thapa being 36 years 11 month 13 days old (D.O.B. 05.12.1974 as mentioned in copy of Election ID Card) will be entitled to loss of future income by applying multiplier of 15 in addition to future prospect @ 40% upon his established income Rs.6,656/- as per minimum wage w.e.f. 01.10.2011 in terms of principles laid down in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi,
(2017) 16 SCC 680.
